en: The Noble Prophecy of Maitreya. Homage to the Noble Maitreya!
Śāriputra, possessed of great wisdom, the sovereign commander of the Dharma army—
Out of compassion for the worlds, he questioned the Teacher.
It was previously declared in another sutra that the teaching of the future Buddha, the Leader of the World, shall indeed be named Maitreya. (Mvyā 2)
Explain that power and also that supernatural might which increases all goals;
we truly desire to hear it, O Leader, supreme among men. (Mvyā 3)
Having heard that, the Blessed One said: "Listen, you, to the manifestation of that best of men, that Buddha Maitreya, as it has been prophesied by me."
At that time, the oceans will dry up on all sides for many yojanas,
and the roads of the universal monarchs will become passable.
At that time, Jambudvīpa was ten thousand yojanas in extent all around; it was the abode of all living beings. (Mvyā 6)
For the men there, as well as their guides, will be doers of good;
they will be non-violent, exempt from punishment, very prosperous, and fortunate.
The ground was free of thorns, level, and dark green; it rose and fell in gentle undulations, soft like cotton wool or fine silk. (Mvyā 8)
Fragrant rice will grow without the need for plowing, sweet and delicious;
and trees that yield garments will appear, adorned with various colors.
The trees will extend for a *krośa* and be bent down by leaves, flowers, and fruits;
and at that time, the lifespan will be exactly eighty thousand years.
Sentient beings will be possessed of fine complexions, strong, and large-bodied;
they will be skillful, free from afflictions, without faults, and long-lived.
There will be three afflictions: desire, old age, and indigestion;
and in the five-hundredth year, a girl shall be married.
At that time, there will be a city there named Ketumatī,
a dwelling for beings who act for the benefit of living creatures.
That city is twelve yojanas long and seven in width; it is meritorious, pure, and delightful.
The lofty walls, made of the seven precious gems, were one *krośa* in width;
they also featured gate-towers and archways adorned with various jewels.
And those moats shall be constructed with bricks made of jewels;
they will be covered with lotuses and water-lilies and adorned with swans.
It was indeed surrounded by rows of trees on all sides;
the palm trees were composed of the four jewels and adorned with networks of tinkling bells.
From those blue jewels, a delightful sound arose, as sweet as a musical instrument endowed with its five components. (Mvyā 18)
And those men in this city who desire the happiness of rest were then gladdened by joyful songs and the sounds of cymbals.
The city built by him shall also be strewn with blue and white lotuses;
these three—the lake, the grove, and the garden—shall come into being.
There, a king named Śaṅkha will arise, possessed of great majesty;
he will be a powerful universal monarch (cakravartin), the sovereign lord of the four continents.
Endowed with the seven precious jewels and as the commander of a fourfold army,
that king will indeed father a thousand sons at that time.
For that lord of men will protect the earth as far as the ocean's edge by means of punishment in accordance with the Dharma, just as it is said.
At that time, the four great treasures of King Śaṅkha were indeed seen by the king,
consisting of hundreds of millions of jewels.
Piṅgala is in Kaliṅga, Pāṇḍuka is in Mithilā, Elapatra is in Gāndhāra, and Śaṅkha is in the city of Vārāṇasī. (Mvyā 25)
Endowed with these four treasures, the king will become a great hero, arisen through the power of a hundred merits.
There will be a brahmin, Subrahmaṇa by name, who is a learned priest of that king; he will be his preceptor, possessing great erudition and mastery of the four Vedas.
He was a teacher, a keeper of the mantras, possessed of memory, and one who had mastered the Vedas;
likewise, he was proficient in the Kaiṭabha lexicon, the Nighaṇṭu, and grammar.
At that time, his wife will be named Brahmāvatī;
she will be beautiful, gracious, handsome, and renowned.
Having descended from the Tuṣita heaven, Maitreya, the foremost of persons,
will certainly take rebirth in her womb.
Then, having carried that one of great splendor for the full ten months,
Maitreya’s mother [gave birth] in this garden filled with beautiful flowers.
Neither sitting nor lying down, that practitioner of the Dharma will stand,
grasping a branch of a tree, and give birth to Maitreya.
The Supreme among Men shall emerge from the right side,
like the sun appearing and radiating light from behind a mass of clouds.
Unstained by the mire of the womb, like a lotus by water,
he will fill this entire triple world with his radiance.
Then the thousand-eyed king of the gods, Śacīpati, being delighted,
was to receive Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds, at the moment of his birth.
As soon as he is born, he will take seven steps;
at every step there shall be a treasure, and at each step a lotus shall appear.
Looking toward the four quarters, he will utter these words:
"This is my final birth; there is no further becoming.
I shall not come to existence again; I shall enter parinirvāṇa, free from outflows."
I shall effect the liberation of those beings who are submerged in the ocean of saṃsāra, who partake in suffering, and who are bound by the fetters of craving.
The gods shall hold a white parasol over his head,
and two lords of the nāgas shall bathe him with streams of cold and warm water.
And having received him— who possesses the thirty-two marks of excellence and blazes with splendor— the nurse will present Maitreya to his mother.
And the deities shall carry her, together with her son, as she ascends a beautiful palanquin adorned with various jewels.
Then, as thousands of musical instruments are being played,
as soon as Maitreya enters that city, a rain of flowers will fall.
Having thus seen his son endowed with the thirty-two excellent marks, Subrahmā will then look back upon the mantras and become joyful.
Two destinies for the prince are seen in the prophecies:
he shall either be a universal monarch, a lord of men, or a Buddha, the supreme among bipeds.
And when that Maitreya, the supreme among men and whose nature is dharma, has reached youth, he will reflect: "Alas, these living beings are indeed suffering."
With a voice like that of Brahmā, a great resonance, the color of gold, and great splendor;
broad-chested, with full shoulders, and eyes resembling lotus petals.
His body will be fifty cubits in height,
and his beautiful complexion and stature will extend for half that measure.
Honored by eighty-four thousand men,
that Maitreya will teach them the mantras.
Then King Śaṅkha will raise up a sacrificial post that is sixteen fathoms wide at its base and one thousand fathoms in height.
Having performed a sacrifice preceded by [all preparations], that lord of men will bestow that sacrificial post, adorned with various jewels, upon the twice-born.
And at the very moment that delightful sacrificial pillar made of jewels is given away,
thousands of brahmins will scatter it about.
Having seen this impermanence of that sacrificial post and having reflected upon the ruin of cyclic existence, Maitreya will take delight in the life of renunciation.
So that, having gone forth here, I may touch the deathless state and liberate the people from the fear of sickness, death, and old age.
Honored by eighty-four thousand followers,
Maitreya, the foremost of persons, will go forth into the homeless life.
At that time, the Nāga tree shall become his Bodhi tree;
its branches will extend fifty yojanas upward.
Sitting beneath it, Maitreya, the Supreme Person and Leader,
shall attain unsurpassed, auspicious enlightenment.
On the very same night that he shall go forth into the homeless life,
on that very same night he will indeed attain supreme enlightenment.
Then that Supreme Person will teach the True Dharma, which removes all suffering and is auspicious, with speech endowed with the eight qualities.
Seeing that the people have become serene, he will proclaim the truths:
suffering, the origin of suffering, and the transcendence of suffering.
And having heard that noble eightfold path, which is secure and leads to Nirvana,
they will also practice that Dharma within the teaching.
In a garden covered with flowers, there will be an assembly;
his retinue will number a full hundred yojanas.
Having heard this, the king, the lord of men named Śaṅkha, who possesses great fame,
will give incalculable gifts and go forth into the homeless life.
Surrounded by eighty-four thousand [attendants],
the lord of men, having gone forth from his home, will enter the religious life.
By this very measure, the father of Maitreya, honored by men, will go forth from home into the religious life there.
Then, there will be a renowned householder named Sudhana;
pure in soul, he will go forth into homelessness under the instruction of Maitreya.
Then there was the jewel among women belonging to Śaṅkha, renowned by the name Viśākhā,
who was attended by eighty-four thousand [followers].
Having gone forth from among women, he will take delight in the religious life.
At that time, hundreds and thousands of living beings will go forth into the homeless life under the instruction of Maitreya.
In this well-flowered garden, there will be a great assembly;
his retinue will extend for a hundred yojanas in every direction.
Then the compassionate Teacher, Maitreya, the Supreme among Men,
having surveyed the assembly, shall proclaim this matter.
All these were seen by the Lion of the Śākyas, the supreme among the virtuous, the Protector, the Lord of the World, who possesses the realm of the True Dharma;
they have been planted on the path to liberation and scattered within my teaching.
Having rendered honor to the stupas with parasols, banners, and flags, and with perfumes, garlands, and ointments, they have indeed come into my presence.
Having given gifts to the Saṅgha— robes, food and drink,
and various medicines for the sick— they have indeed come into my presence.
Having offered a sprinkling of saffron water and an anointing with sandalwood paste at the stupas of Śākyamuni, they have indeed come into my presence.
Having undertaken the precepts within the teaching of the Lion of the Śākyas,
protect them according to reality, for you have come into my presence.
Having observed here the auspicious noble eightfold fast (upoṣadha) on the fourteenth,
the fifteenth, and likewise the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles, one should remain well-composed in this eightfold [vow].
Having undertaken the precepts and attained the teaching,
those beings who have gone to the instruction [of the Buddha] take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
And having performed wholesome deeds, they have come to my teaching.
Therefore, these beings were sent by him, and they have also been established by me;
they have been embraced by that best of assemblies, the Sage of vast intelligence.
Seeing the people with serene minds, he will proclaim the truths;
and having heard the Dharma from him, they will attain the supreme state.
By means of the three miracles, he will discipline the disciples;
there, all those well-behaved ones will exhaust their outflows.
His first assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-six billion followers who have severed the cycle of existence.
His second assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-four billion who are peaceful and possessed of vast wisdom.
His third assembly of disciples will consist of twenty-two full koṭis of those who are peaceful and whose minds are tranquil.
Then, having set in motion the wheel of Dharma and having disciplined gods and humans,
he will wander for alms in the city together with the community of disciples.
Then, as he enters that beautiful city of Ketumatī,
Māndārava flowers will fall upon that supreme city.
The deities will scatter [flowers] when the Sage has entered that city.
The four great kings and Śakra, the lord of the thirty-three gods,
as well as Brahmā together with the hosts of deities, shall perform worship for him.
Blue lotuses, white water-lilies, red lotuses, and white lotuses, as well as fragrant flowers,
aloe-wood, sandalwood, and divine garlands shall fall down.
The sons of the gods, possessed of great supernatural power,
will wave their garments as they gaze upon that Lord of the World entering the supreme city.
And a divine sound of musical instruments and divine garlands shall fall;
the deities will scatter them as the Sage enters that city.
And those humans who shall dwell in Ketumatī will also worship him as he enters that supreme city.
Then, upon that path, they will scatter a ground-covering soft as cotton-wool, as well as various beautiful garlands. (Mvyā 89)
With parasols, banners, and flags, humans shall worship [it],
and with the auspicious sounds of musical instruments, men shall do so with serene minds.
And Śakra, the thousand-eyed king of the gods and lord of Śacī,
being greatly delighted and with palms joined in reverence, shall praise the Jina Maitreya.
Homage to you, O noble among men; homage to you, O supreme among men!
Have compassion for the people, O Blessed One, O foremost of persons. (Mvyā 92)
A son of the gods possessed of great supernatural power will become his Māra;
and he too, with palms joined in reverence, will offer praise to the Leader of the World.
Surrounded by many thousands of Śuddhāvāsa deities,
Maitreya, the Lord of the World and Guide, shall enter.
Surrounded by a retinue of Brahmās, Brahmā himself shall also proclaim the True Dharma with clear speech, uttering the Brahmā-sound.
The entire earth will be filled with Arhats—
those whose taints are exhausted, who have vomited out their faults, and for whom the bonds of existence have been abandoned.
The gods and humans, the gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, as well as the nāgas of great supernatural power, will all be delighted and perform worship to the Teacher.
They will surely become free from sin, with their doubts severed;
wise ones who have cast away the moat [of craving], who grasp at nothing, and who are free from longing.
And they shall practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They too will surely be without "mine-ness" and without possessions; they will be without gold or silver, homeless, and free from social attachment—
those who shall practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
Having severed the very net with their own arms, they will indeed go to the further shore;
having attained the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) and being endowed with joy and bliss,
they will practice the holy life (brahmacarya) under the instruction of Maitreya.
For sixty thousand years, Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds and the Teacher, will proclaim the true Dharma out of compassion for the world.
Having disciplined hundreds and thousands of living beings through his Dharma-body, that Leader will then enter nirvāṇa.
And when that wise Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds, has passed into nirvāṇa,
the true Dharma shall remain on earth for ten thousand years.
They gladden their minds toward the Victor Śākyamuni;
therefore, you shall behold Maitreya, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds.
Therefore, by clarifying one's mind toward the Dharma, the Buddha, and the Sangha, the supreme assembly, one will become possessed of great supernatural power.
Having propitiated that compassionate Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds,
at the proper time, you shall thereafter attain nirvāṇa.
Having heard this wonder and having seen even such small manifestations of power,
what wise person would not be inspired with faith, even among those born into dark births?
Therefore, one who desires self-benefit here and aspires to greatness should honor the True Dharma, remembering the teaching of the Buddha. (Mvyā 108)
The Prophecy of Maitreya is completed.
